- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% relative to prior peak.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.67), model underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% to reflect risk-off reversal.
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days) — cap forecast growth at 3–4% after spike, unless sentiment confirms continuation.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, model often fails to correct — add 0.5–1.5% upward bias to counteract.
- For 30-day horizon, model underestimates true price by 1–4% in 70%+ of cases — apply +1.5% to forecast if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– swings (e.g., +0.67, -0.67, +0.67), model tends to lag — add 0.5–1.0% to forecast to catch momentum.
- Avoid “overfitting to recent highs” — if last 3–5 prices are rising, don’t assume 30d will continue — cap forecast at 1–2% below recent 5-day high unless sentiment confirms breakout.
